meta.title: San Diego County — November 3, 2026 General Election Ballot
meta.heading: OFFICIAL BALLOT — STATEWIDE GENERAL ELECTION
meta.subheading: NOVEMBER 3, 2026 · SAN DIEGO COUNTY, CALIFORNIA · CA-50 · AD-78 · SUPERVISOR D4 · COUNCIL D2
meta.disclaimer: Finalists from certified June 2 results and your printed ballot — verify against your official sample ballot. Corruption notes from search summaries; details in corruption-*.md.

rules.title: 1. No corruption
rules.detail: ethics findings, fines, settlements, probes (old/cleared = borderline)

rules.title: 3. No fossil-fuel expansion
rules.detail: no more oil/gas or weaker environmental review

rules.title: 4. Anti-gun
rules.detail: no pro-gun records or gun-group endorsements

rules.title: 5. No tax increases — except on billionaires
rules.detail: billionaire taxes OK; blocking them counts against

rules.title: 6. Not housing-first
rules.detail: building housing isn't the main homelessness fix

rules_footer: When every option breaks a rule, the pick is marked "Lean" (toss-up). Leaving a race blank is always an option.

candidates.name: Xavier Becerra
candidates.title: Voting Rights Attorney (former U.S. HHS Secretary)
pros: Not on any of your June filter lists
Homelessness: accountability for funding; no voluntary homelessness when shelter offered
cons: Wants to extend higher tax rates on top earners
Opposes the billionaire tax (Prop 40), which your rules allow
Open to weakening clean-energy goals / 2035 gas-car ban if fuel gets costly
Housing emergency + zoning push (supply-leaning)
candidates.corruption: MINOR — Victim (not suspect) of ~$225K stolen from his dormant campaign account by ex-Newsom chief of staff (guilty plea May 2026). 2023 Office of Special Counsel found a Hatch Act violation (endorsed Padilla at an official event).

best.why: Hilton fails fossil-fuel and gun rules; Becerra's ethics issue is as a victim.

candidates.name: Steve Hilton
candidates.title: Small Business Owner (commentator, ex-adviser to UK PM)
pros: Tax cuts: no income tax on first $150K, halve gas tax
Not housing-first: clear encampments, sober housing
cons: Pro fossil fuel: more oil & gas, end renewable mandates
Pro-guns: loosen firearm restrictions
candidates.corruption: CLEAN — nothing found.

candidates.corruption: MINOR, borderline SERIOUS — $350K state-paid settlement of harassment suit (denied, not adjudicated); donor ties to China school accused of diploma fraud; support letter for convicted briber Ken Hong Wong. Nothing proven.

best.why: Toss-up. Ma has real ethics baggage; Romero's pro-gun flag is party-based only and Lt. Gov has little say on guns.

items.text: ★ Recommendation: YES on all 17 justices — every one came back CLEAN (no Commission on Judicial Performance discipline, scandals or controversies) and no campaign exists against any of them. Judges cannot take positions on your issues, so rule 1 (corruption) is the test. A No vote lets the governor appoint the replacement.

items.title: Proposition 1
items.subtitle: Housing Affordability Bonds
items.summary: $11.25B bond for affordable rentals, supportive housing, veterans' home loans and down-payment help. Cost: $500–600M/yr for ~25 years.
pros: Funds veterans' housing and supportive housing
cons: Housing-first-style funding
Adds state debt
items.money: Airbnb $1M, carpenters $1M, Building a Better California $1M. No opposition filed.

rec.why: Housing-first-style spending plus $500–600M/yr in new debt.

items.title: Proposition 2
items.subtitle: Increases State's Rainy Day Fund
items.summary: Changes reserve deposit limits and debt-paydown rules; state reserves would be higher.
items.money: Backed by Newsom, Becerra, firefighters. No opposition.

rec.why: Bigger reserves, no tax; nothing against your priorities.

items.title: Proposition 3
items.subtitle: Permanent Tax on High Incomes
items.summary: Makes the income tax on earners above ~$371K permanent instead of expiring in 2031. Keeps $5–15B/yr for schools and health care.
cons: Permanent tax increase (your tax filter)

items.title: Proposition 4
items.subtitle: Public Funding of Election Campaigns
items.summary: Lets state and local governments create public campaign-financing programs.
pros: Anti-corruption: reduces reliance on big donors
Backed by League of Women Voters, Consumer Watchdog
cons: Uses public money for campaigns

rec.why: Anti-corruption: less dependence on big donors.

items.title: Proposition 5
items.subtitle: Recall Election Process
items.summary: Removes the replacement question from recall ballots; vacancy filled by special election or appointment.
pros: Prevents a replacement winning with a tiny plurality
cons: Voters lose direct choice of replacement on recall day
items.money: Backed by LWV and Common Cause. No opposition.

rec.why: Not tied to your priorities; good-government groups back it, no opposition.

items.title: Proposition 37
items.subtitle: Middle-Income New-Home Loans
items.summary: Up to $25B in revenue bonds for fixed-rate mortgages on new homes under ~$1.5M. No direct state cost.
pros: Homeownership help at no taxpayer cost
cons: Mainly benefits the realtors and builders paying for it
Demand subsidy could push prices up
items.money: CA Realtors $14.85M, Building a Better California $6M, carpenters.

rec.why: Benefits the realtors and builders funding it; not a homelessness fix.

items.title: Proposition 38
items.subtitle: Immunology Research Bonds
items.summary: $8.4B bond for immunology research. Cost: $500–600M/yr for ~20 years.
pros: Research on immune diseases and cancer
cons: Adds $8.4B debt
items.money: Self-dealing concern (CalMatters): rules fit only one institute (CIIT), chaired by top funder Gary Michelson, who gave ~$18–19M.

items.title: Proposition 39
items.subtitle: Voter Identification
items.summary: Government ID required to vote in person; last four digits of an ID number on mail ballots.
cons: Costs tens to hundreds of millions/yr
May block some eligible voters
items.money: $17M from Richard Uihlein (Trump-aligned Illinois billionaire), $3.1M Reform California. Against: ACLU, Common Cause, LWV.

rec.why: Not tied to your priorities; costs taxpayers yearly and is bankrolled by the Reform California network.

items.title: Proposition 40
items.subtitle: One-Time Tax on Billionaires
items.summary: One-time 5% tax on wealth over $1B (~200 people), ~90% to health care.
pros: Taxes only billionaires — OK under your rules
Funds health care from the ultra-wealthy only
cons: Billionaires may leave, cutting future income-tax revenue
items.money: For: SEIU-UHW $32M (has spent ~$125M on ballot measures since 2012). Against: $88.5M+ — Building a Better California is funded by tech billionaires (Sergey Brin largest, plus Doerr, Thiel, Levchin, Collison and others).

rec.why: Taxes only ~200 billionaires — allowed under your rules; funds health care.

items.title: Proposition 41
items.subtitle: No Taxes Exempt from Spending Limit
items.summary: Voids post-2026 state taxes exempt from the spending limit; State Auditor reviews special-tax programs.
pros: Limits some future taxes on everyone
cons: Written to kill billionaire taxes like Prop 40 (allowed by your rules)
items.money: $58M from Building a Better California is funded by tech billionaires (Sergey Brin largest, plus Doerr, Thiel, Levchin, Collison and others).

rec.why: Written to void billionaire taxes like Prop 40; paid for by the billionaires it protects.

items.title: Proposition 42
items.subtitle: Ban State Wealth / Personal Property Taxes
items.summary: Bans new state wealth (personal property) taxes and certain retroactive taxes.
cons: Bans billionaire wealth taxes (allowed by your rules)
Biggest one-funder campaign on the ballot, paid for by those it protects
items.money: $98M from Building a Better California is funded by tech billionaires (Sergey Brin largest, plus Doerr, Thiel, Levchin, Collison and others).

rec.why: Bans billionaire wealth taxes, which your rules allow; $98M from the billionaires it protects.

items.title: Proposition 43
items.subtitle: Two-Thirds for Local Special Taxes
items.summary: Certain local special taxes need two-thirds instead of a majority, starting 2027.
pros: Makes local tax increases harder (your tax filter)
cons: Could limit local fire, transit and homelessness funding
items.money: CA Business Roundtable $9.85M, Kilroy Realty $1M. Against: firefighters, teachers, SEIU.

items.text: CARD B · BACK (not in your photos — verify)

items.title: Proposition 44
items.subtitle: Clinics Must Spend 90% on Services
items.summary: Nonprofit community health clinics must spend at least 90% of revenue on program services.
cons: Opposed by doctors, pediatricians and Family Health Centers of San Diego
Similar bill already failed
items.money: SEIU funds 100% of Yes ($16.9M); clinics (AltaMed etc.) fund No.

rec.why: Union-vs-clinic fight; local clinics and doctors oppose.

items.title: Proposition 45
items.subtitle: CEQA Environmental Review Changes
items.summary: Deadlines and limits on environmental review and lawsuits for housing, transit, water, clean-energy and wildfire projects.
pros: Faster clean-energy, transit and wildfire projects
cons: Weakens environmental review (climate groups oppose)
Build-more housing approach
items.money: Building a Better California $10M, Building Industry Assn $5.65M. Against: Coalition for Clean Air, CA Environmental Voters.

items.title: County of San Diego — Measure A
items.subtitle: Charter Amendment
items.summary: Independent ethics commission, budget analyst and auditor; confirmation of senior county leaders; spending disclosure; supervisor term limits raised from two to three terms.
cons: Extends term limits for the sitting supervisors who put it on the ballot
items.money: Yes $45K, No $0. Self-interest on the term-limit piece.

rec.why: Ethics commission and auditor outweigh the term-limit extension.

items.title: County of San Diego — Measure B
items.subtitle: Health & Safety Act
items.summary: Permanent half-cent countywide sales tax (~$400–450M/yr): 60% health, child care and food; 22.5% Tijuana River sewage; 17.5% wildfire and public safety.
pros: Fixes Tijuana River sewage; wildfire funding
cons: Permanent sales-tax increase with no end date (your tax filter)
items.money: Yes $2.3M (hospital association, SEIU, Dems — groups that receive the money) vs No $149K (Taxpayers Assn, Reform California).

items.title: San Diego Unified — School Facilities Bond (reported as Measure M)
items.summary: $3.5B in bonds for school facilities, about $32 per $100,000 of assessed value. Needs 55%.
pros: School repairs; district says the tax rate won't rise above current
cons: $3.5B property-tax-backed debt
items.money: Backed by Taxpayers Assn, teachers union, Dems. No organized opposition.
